q: Is all the CO2 from burning tyre-derived fuel fossil?
title: Tyre-derived fuel and biogenic carbon
short: No. Tyres contain natural rubber, which is biogenic, along with synthetic rubber and carbon black, which are fossil. Only the fossil share counts as Scope 1 CO2; the biogenic share is reported separately. Ask the supplier or a lab for the fossil carbon fraction rather than assuming one.
audience: Cement kilns, boilers and pyrolysis plants using tyre fuels

ul: Calorific value and carbon content from lab tests.
The fossil and biogenic split, with its source.

p: For covered goods, the biomass share of a mixed fuel must be supported by evidence before it can be treated as zero rated.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
